The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 3/4/2019 Ramkishan Singh Tomar vs Munshi Singh Yadav on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148570654/
1 passed by Ninth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in MACC No.236/2018 by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.5,49,630/- with 7%
interest to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 18/7/2017..
2.

sentences.text: According to claimant, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side, hence needs to be enhanced.
So the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal on facts/ evidence adduced is made out and if so to what extent?
3. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that all these findings are recorded in favour of claimants by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in favour of claimants are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of cross-appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden the judgment by detailing facts on all these issues.
4. As observed supra, it is an injury case.

On 18/7/2017, appellant met with a road accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No. 1- dumper driver and sustained fracture in hand and injuries in head and other parts of the body which gave rise to filing of claim petition, out of which this appeal arises seeking enhancement of compensation.
The case was contested by the respondents.
Parties adduced evidence.
The Claims Tribunal by impugned award partly allowed the claim petition filed by claimants and, as stated supra, awarded a sum of Rs.5,49,630/-.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Claims Tribunal assessed the extent of disability to 30%; whereas, in the accident his one hand got fully non-functional and therefore, same was liable to be assessed at 100%.
The income assessed by the tribunal is on lower side which needs to be assessed properly.
It is also submitted that the amount awarded by the tribunal under the other heads is also on lower side.
Hence prayed that the appeal be allowed and amount of compensation be enhanced substantially.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance company submits that the amount awarded by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no case for enhancement is made out.
Hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. From perusal of the record as well as para 18 to 20 of impugned award, the findings given by Claims Tribunal in assessing the extent of disability to 30% appears to be just and proper and needs no interference.

It is further evident that in absence of any documentary evidence, the Claims Tribunal assessed the income of appellant at Rs. 5,000/- which also appears to be just and proper and the amount awarded under conventional heads also appears to be just and proper and in line of pleadings and evidence put forth before the Claims Tribunal.
Ramkishan Singh Tomar vs Munshi Singh Yadav on 12 April, 2024

Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal adopted a lenient approach in awarded an amount of Rs.5,49,630/- as compensation which is found just and proper and needs no interference.
9. Hence, the appeal is hereby dismissed.
